internal_decisions: parse_amount uses re.fullmatch on the stripped text, with [0-9] so only ASCII digits match.
Strings such as '1.' and '.5' are rejected, because the spec requires digits before the dot and one or two digits after it.

internal_decisions: parse_date matches [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} with fullmatch, so it rejects non-ASCII digits and a trailing newline
month_end computes the first day of the next month and subtracts one day

plan: Baseline: tests (34) and acceptance (19) all pass.
Contracts: ledger→money/dates/settle boundaries covered in qa/test_qa.py (balances sum to 0, settle accepts ledger output, input dict unchanged, ≤ n-1 transfers).
Integration: random 60-expense ledger → period balances → settle → net zero.

Edge cases: odd amount/date strings (trailing newline, unicode digits, '1.', '+5'), split properties over 500 random cases, atomic failed add, no aliasing of the participants list, frozen Expense, empty period, start>end in balances, settle({}).
Regression: discarded, nothing existed before this architecture apart from the version test.
Non-functional: discarded, the architecture names no security or performance requirements.
Rerun: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa (12 tests, all green; no defects found, so no test is red on purpose).
gaps: Dates at the datetime.date upper bound (9999-12) would probably raise OverflowError from month_end. The contract does not cover this, so I did not test it.
Non-str or non-int arguments (e.g. float parts, None text) are outside the section 6 contract and were not tested.
No linter, type checker or formatter is configured in the repo, so no static analysis was run.

advisory.problem: AC-011 'a failed add changes nothing' is only checked once, on a ledger that was empty before. A partial-write bug is caught only if it registers a name. It would not be caught if a bad add stored the expense but still left balances() empty, which is unlikely.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that appends to the list before validating the last field would still be caught by balances(). Only a state that balances() cannot see would slip through.

advisory.problem: AC-010 does not check that Expense is frozen, which the data model requires. The criterion does not list it, so this is only a note.
